title: Tenant-level tail visibility playbook for console ingress and KV cache
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Summary: During a recent capacity/regression incident on 2025-01-30 the console experienced intermittent tail latency spikes and short-lived routing backpressure for a small set of tenants. The incident was resolved via temporary routing fallback, but root cause analysis found multiple observability blind spots: aggregate percentiles masked per-tenant extrema, eviction events from the KV cache weren't exposed per-tenant, and tracing sampling dropped critical spans when CPU saturation occurred. Goal: deliver a playbook and implementation plan to surface tenant-level tail signals, add targeted instrumentation for KV eviction/queue depth, redesign dashboards and alerts, and bake a lightweight canary to detect regressions before customer impact.
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant 99th/99.9th and max latency metrics emitted for all console ingress routes
KV cache exports eviction_count and eviction_last_timestamp tagged by tenant and pool
New heatmap dashboard for tenant tail latency by route and pool is available in Grafana
Alerts exist for per-tenant queue depth and per-tenant 99.9th exceeding thresholds
Tracing preserved for high-latency requests via adaptive sampling policy and tenant tags
Runbook updated with steps to isolate high-tail tenants and cache remediation play
Canary tenant traffic generator running nightly exercising cache fill/evict and observed by dashboards
action_items: Instrument per-tenant metrics: add labels tenant_id and pool to ingress_latency_histogram and expose 99.9th and max
Emit KV cache eviction metrics: eviction_count, eviction_reason, eviction_last_ts with tenant tag
Add tenant tag propagation to tracing context and increase sampling for requests with eviction header
New Grafana dashboard: tenant-tail-heatmap, route split, kv-eviction-trends, queue-depth-by-tenant
Create PagerDuty alert: per-tenant queued_requests > 100 for 1m OR per-tenant p99.9 > 2s for 5m
Implement synthetic canary: nightly job that simulates 1000 requests for a designated canary tenant including cache churn scenarios
Document runbook steps: identify tenant, fallback to variant model, force cache warm, escalate to infra
Add telemetry contract to CI: require exported metrics for any change touching routing, cache, or ingress handlers
Post-deploy smoke: run quick tenant-scan to validate per-tenant metrics available after rollout
